description: The function that turns attention scores into weights.
text: Softmax The softmax of a vector of scores is the exponential of each score divided by the sum of the exponentials. The trap Large scores overflow the exponential. Self-attention subtracts the row maximum first. Why subtract the maximum before the softmax? It keeps the exponentials finite and leaves the result unchanged.
title: Softmax

description: Where the cost of self-attention comes from, for someone who knows matrix products.
text: Every token scores against every other token, so the cost grows with the square of the length. Where the scores come from In self-attention each query meets every key. Where the weights come from Each row of scores goes through a softmax . Why does a longer context cost more than it adds? Every new token scores against all the others.

description: The number of points is varied; the RMS error over 100 seeds is measured.
text: Hypothesis The RMS error of the estimate falls as one over the square root of the number of points. Intuition Each point is an independent draw, inside the quarter circle or not. The one variable The number of points: 64, 256, 1,024, 4,096 and 16,384. Held fixed The estimator, the random generator and the seeds. Pinned configuration Allowed moves Nothing under test makes moves. Measures The RMS error over 100 seeds, per size, and the log-log slope across sizes. Decision rules D1: a slope between -0.6 and -0.4 keeps the hypothesis. D2 (kill): an error that does not shrink drops it. Predictions P1: the slope lies between -0.55 and -0.45. Confidence: 85%. What it cannot show Anything about another estimator.
title: How the error of the pi estimate scales with the sample size

description: Convincing on translation, silent on long contexts.
text: What it claims Self-attention links any two positions in a constant number of steps, where a recurrent layer needs as many steps as the sequence is long. My take It holds for short sequences. It agrees with our softmax page. Why does the paper scale the dot products? Large dot products push the softmax into regions with tiny gradients.
title: Attention Is All You Need

description: The RMS error of a Monte Carlo estimate of pi, at five sample sizes.
text: The question, in words Does the error of the estimate shrink as one over the square root of the sample size? What we expected, and why The protocol expected the square-root law. What we did We ran the estimator at every size. What happened The law held (R-4 ). What we learned The slope pools every size, so it is a robust test. What this does not show Anything about another estimator.
